# Starship Troopers: Ultimate Bug War!

Starship Troopers: Ultimate Bug War! is a first-person shooter developed by Bristol-based Auroch Digital and published by DotEmu.  Released on March 16, 2026, the game is a licensed adaptation of the Starship Troopers franchise, drawing inspiration from Robert A. Heinlein's 1959 novel and Paul Verhoeven's 1997 film.  It features high-mobility combat between the human Federation and insectoid "Bugs," presented in a "boomer shooter" style that utilises a low-fidelity aesthetic melding 3D environments with 2D character sprites.
Gameplay
The game's campaign is framed as a "faithful training simulation" developed by the United Citizen Federation's state-sponsored developer, FedDev.
Set approximately 25 years after the "First Bug War," the plot follows Major Samantha "Sammy" Dietz (portrayed by Charlotta) as she recounts her hunt for the Assassin Bug across eight missions.  Missions take place on iconic series locations including Klendathu, Planet P, and Zegema Beach.
Combat emphasises "swarm" mechanics, with players facing standard Warrior bugs and Aphids alongside specialised units like Tankers and Centurions.  The arsenal includes 14 weapons, such as the Morita assault rifle, and 11 "Tactical Supports" like orbital strikes and mechanical bipeds.  The game includes four difficulty settings, a "God Mode," and specialised control options like a "Joy-Con mouse mode" for the Nintendo Switch version.
Movement is influenced by a stamina-based sprint mechanic, while a squad system allows players to rally AI-controlled allies, however, permanently enabled friendly fire often leads to accidental casualties during chaotic encounters.
A secondary "Bug Mode" features five missions where players control a "simulated" Assassin Bug.  These shorter missions function as a power fantasy, allowing players to rampage through Federation forces with the ability to fly, spit acid and rally other bugs by approaching their hives.  In-game lore suggests these missions are another form of Federation propaganda designed to entice recruits.
Development
Auroch Digital developed the title following their work on Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun.  The narrative is presented through live-action Full Motion Video (FMV) sequences, a design choice inspired by 1990s titles such as Command & Conquer.
These sequences feature Casper Van Dien reprising his role as Johnny Rico, who is now a General and eye-patch-wearing veteran, who introduces the player to Major Dietz.  Between levels, the game includes satirical advertisements and propaganda shorts intended to replicate the tone of the 1997 film.  Stéphane Pérez, the FMV director, collaborated with the "Starship Troopers German Division" fan community to ensure the accuracy of the costumes used in filming.
Reception
Following a demo period that saw a 92% positive rating on Steam, the full release received generally favourable reviews.
Critics praised the satirical tone and faithful recreation of the franchise's militaristic aesthetic.
The Jimquisition lauded the game's presentation, while PC Gamer highlighted the chaotic intensity of the swarm combat.  While the human campaign was well-received, some reviewers found the Bug Mode missions to be somewhat "janky" and less engaging by comparison.
